answer: We formulate a decentralized mechanism incorporating dynamic opportunity-cost bonds and subgame-perfect slashing matrices, where agents posting cedar reserves face timber penalties for Sybil identities. At each vertex of the strategy space, expected payoff of identity multiplication is strictly negative, rendering Sybil attacks unprofitable. In adversarial multi-agent environments, this mechanism guarantees strict Nash equilibrium convergence, as rational agents optimally choose not to proliferate identities, thereby ensuring robustness against Sybil manipulation.
